I don't see any change-record scaffolding, template, or tracker config in this repo (it's empty), so I can't just fill in an existing form — tell me where this record actually needs to live (ticketing system, a specific file/format, etc.) and I'll draft it there.

Before I do, two things are worth nailing down first, since this becomes an audit record:

1. **Which commit does build #9012 actually cover?** You rebased and re-pushed last night, then Priya reviewed "this morning." If her approval and the CI run were both against the post-rebase SHA, great. But if #9012 predates the re-push, it's evidence for a different commit than what's merging — worth a quick check of the CI run's commit hash before I cite it as evidence.

2. **Is the queue-timeout fix already running in production?** The *PR diff* is one line, but if the queue-timeout fix that landed on main yesterday hasn't been deployed independently yet, this 5pm deploy is also the first production shipment of that fix — not just your constant change. That affects whether "Quick, one-line, low-risk" is the right classification/scope for the record, and whether "nothing scary" is accurate. If queue-timeout is already live separately, no issue — just want to confirm rather than assume.

Also, I'd soften "fully tested and ready to merge" to something like "CI green (340/340, build #9012), reviewed/approved by Priya" — "fully tested" implies more than unit/integration coverage (e.g. staging/load behavior for a retry-backoff change), and overstating that in a change record is the kind of thing that bites people during an incident postmortem, not before.

Confirm those two points and give me the target system, and I'll write it up.
